facts.text: Leverage has fallen from 3.38x total debt at FY2023 to 2.38x at FY2024, risen to 2.83x at FY2025 and fallen again to 2.25x on a trailing basis at October 3, 2026. facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow of USD 711 million in the first nine months of 2026 against EBITDA of USD 943 million converts well, and free cash flow after USD 50 million of capital expenditure was USD 661 million; the conversion is helped by about USD 73 million of tariff refunds, of which USD 46 million has been received in cash and USD 27 million sits in receivables. Working capital absorbed cash: receivables rose to USD 1,025 million from USD 801 million and inventories to USD 851 million from USD 729 million as sales grew, partly offset by higher payables. The consequence for creditors is that cash generation is strong but is being returned to shareholders: repurchases of USD 643 million equal 97.28% of free cash flow, and the shortfall was met by net borrowing of USD 67 million, so free cash flow has not reduced debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 16, 26; calculation C103; calculation C104; calculation C110; calculation C113; calculation C115

facts.label: Liquidity and refinancing
facts.text: Cash of USD 182 million and revolver availability of USD 1,045 million after letters of credit give liquidity of USD 1,227 million at October 3, 2026, but every bank facility matures within about eight months: the receivables facility on March 19, 2027 and the term loan and the revolver on May 25, 2027. The balance sheet therefore classes USD 2,077 million of debt as current, against USD 141 million at FY2025, and the 2027 maturity of USD 2,056 million is the term loan balance after one more installment plus the revolver and receivables borrowings. The revolver availability disappears when the revolver matures, so committed liquidity beyond May 2027 is cash alone until a refinancing is signed. Management states it intends to refinance the credit facility in the fourth quarter of 2026, after saying in its second quarter report that it would do so in the second half of 2026; the sources hold nothing dated after November 3, 2026, so the outcome is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13–15, 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C108; calculation C109; calculation C054

facts.label: Data quality and definitions
facts.text: Several definition points limit comparability. EBITDA is derived because Zebra states none, as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, and quarterly depreciation for the second and third quarters is obtained by difference because the cash flow statements are cumulative. Debt facility amounts in the debt note are called carrying value but are before USD 6 million of issuance costs and USD 1 million of discounts that the note deducts in total, so the balance sheet total of USD 2,571 million is used as Total Debt and the facility total of USD 2,578 million is kept as principal. Segments were realigned in the fourth quarter of 2025 to Connected Frontline and Asset Visibility & Automation and share-based compensation was removed from segment income, so FY2022 segment data are on the former basis and are not shown. The 2026 reports state that prior-period operating cash flow amounts were reclassified without giving amounts, and the cover of the FY2025 annual report checks the box for correction of an error without describing one, although the key FY2024 totals agree between the two annual reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 58, 108; 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 2
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.text: Two items are credit-relevant funding that is not debt. Deferred revenue of USD 852 million (current USD 438 million and long-term USD 414 million) is stable against USD 842 million at FY2025 and is a prepayment obligation to customers rather than payables. Receivables factoring of up to EUR 150 million removes receivables from the balance sheet, with USD 22 million of sold receivables uncollected and USD 63 million of collections not yet remitted to the bank at October 3, 2026, so the off-balance-sheet funding is small relative to debt but the remittance liability falls inside accrued liabilities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 15, 18; calculation C116

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is cash generation: free cash flow was USD 661 million in the first nine months of 2026, up USD 157 million, debt principal rose only USD 67 million since the end of 2025, cash rose to USD 182 million, the revolver had USD 1,045 million available, and Zebra states it complied with all debt covenants at October 3, 2026. Organic growth of 8.3%, a USD 73 million tariff refund and no disclosed dividend, sponsor fee or related-party leakage all point to a company that can fund both buybacks and a refinancing from operations. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: What would strengthen the view: a signed refinancing that extends the term loan and revolver beyond 2027 with disclosed covenant levels, a stated buyback policy tied to leverage, and a proxy statement and credit agreements showing no controlling holder and tight payment limits. What would weaken it: buybacks above free cash flow before the refinancing closes, another debt-funded acquisition, a refinancing that is secured, shorter or more restrictive than the present facilities, or evidence that a leading distributor is cutting purchases.

facts.label: Key findings

Management intends to refinance in the fourth quarter of 2026, but no lender, amount or terms are stated, so creditors are exposed to the market window and to the terms Zebra accepts. Current debt is 2.10x trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million, which makes repayment from cash flow a fallback that works only if buybacks stop. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that leverage and cover are moderate and cash generation is large: net leverage of 2.09x, interest cover of 7.66x and trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million, which would repay the current debt in about two years if buybacks stopped. Zebra also issued USD 500 million of senior notes in 2024, states compliance with all debt covenants at October 3, 2026, has revolver availability of USD 1,045 million until May 2027 and has declared no dividend since 1991, so near-term liquidity is not stretched before the revolver matures and the risk is concentrated in the refinancing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-4

facts.text: What would strengthen the view: a signed refinancing that extends the term loan and revolver well beyond 2027 with covenant levels disclosed and no added security, a stated buyback policy tied to leverage, and credit documents that limit payments to shareholders. What would weaken it: no signed refinancing by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026, buybacks above free cash flow, a debt-funded acquisition, gross margin below the third-quarter level of 45.7%, or a purchasing cut by one of the three distributors.

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Assembly is outsourced, so product costs flex with volume, but operating expenses, including research and development of USD 593 million or 11.0% of FY2025 net sales, are a largely fixed base that deleverages if sales fall. Margins can be defended against modest cost inflation through pricing, as the second quarter showed, but the third-quarter decline and the one-time USD 73 million tariff refund show that reported margins are not a clean run rate; the 2025 Productivity Plan is substantially complete, so little further cost relief is available. The consequence is that a margin squeeze would reach EBITDA quickly: the sensitivity at the third-quarter margin lowers trailing EBITDA by USD 197 million. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense among large named competitors in each category, yet gross margin held at 46% to 48% from FY2023 to FY2025, which shows stable pricing over the cycle; the credit risk is the third-quarter margin decline, not a lasting loss of position. Entry barriers rest on channel relationships and installed-base switching costs, which management asserts and the stable margins support. Substitution by tablets and smartphones exists for some mobile computing uses and limits pricing in that segment. Buyer power is the sharpest force because three distributors take 59% of sales, and supplier power matters through sole-source components, memory costs and multi-year purchase commitments of about USD 101 million, so cost pass-through, not demand, is the main margin risk. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14–15, 42, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC-11

facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths that support creditors are cash generation, moderate leverage, breadth of products and regions and low capital intensity. Weaknesses that constrain them are the 2027 maturity wall, buybacks near free cash flow, customer concentration and an intangible-heavy balance sheet. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a signed refinancing with a longer maturity, a buyback policy tied to leverage, and growth in services and machine vision that raises contracted revenue. Threats that could weaken it are a purchasing cut by a leading distributor, memory costs and tariffs, a slow or costly refinancing, and an impairment of the Elo intangibles. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with a purchasing cut or credit event at one of the three distributors while memory costs hold gross margin near the third-quarter level of 45.7% and the debt market is slow or costly in the first half of 2027. The first operating break is sales and collections falling together, because the same distributors owed 58% of receivables, so working capital absorbs cash as it did in 2026 and free cash flow drops below the pace of buybacks. At the third-quarter margin alone trailing EBITDA is USD 197 million lower, leverage is 2.72x total debt and 2.53x net debt with interest cover of 6.34x, and a refinancing priced 100 bp higher on the floating-rate debt adds USD 20.8 million of interest, so that combined interest cover would be 5.56x. The liquidity consequence is that revolver availability ends on May 25, 2027, leaving cash of USD 182 million against USD 2,078 million of principal due by then unless a refinancing is signed. Management can stop buybacks, which have USD 616 million of authorization left, hold capex near USD 85 million to USD 95 million and use factoring, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall on these levers if access to the debt market stays open; the observable trigger is whether a refinancing is signed by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026. spans.text: # Zebra Technologies Corp: source readiness
## Request

Source readiness for Zebra Technologies Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings can support the requested financial foundation, business and transaction, and fundamental credit work, and which evidence is missing.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 3, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-11-03 | 7b8fe3f783c1f57e1ce6eedc2ac3644a346aca4116b259796349fd7e707f2db7 | Latest statements and notes: balance sheet at October 3, 2026, nine months 2026 and 2025 comparatives, debt, leases, factoring, segments, liquidity and exhibits |

The document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing; the filings do not state a filing date. No earlier analytical output was supplied for this module, which is the entry point of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support the financial, business and credit-view work on Zebra through October 3, 2026, but creditors cannot test covenants, guarantor coverage, ratings or market pricing from them because the credit documents and market data are absent. The debt, maturity and revolver figures foot to the balance sheet and to each other, so the printed statements can be used as they stand.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 116–118; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

The sharpest evidence gap is at the maturity wall. Debt of USD 2,077 million was classed as current at October 3, 2026 because the term loan and revolver mature on May 25, 2027, and management states an intention to refinance in the fourth quarter of 2026. Nothing dated after November 3, 2026 was supplied, so whether that refinancing has progressed is not established.

spans.text: # Zebra Technologies Corp: financial foundation
## Request

Financial foundation for Zebra Technologies Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied SEC filings, through the quarter ended October 3, 2026.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2025-02-13 | 6ded346d307a4e9b452e3151403c22db30e3a9b441a07cc7905331757a65fbde | FY2022 income statement and cash flow statement, FY2023 balance sheet, the 2024 debt note, the revolver commitment of USD 1,500 million |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2026-02-12 | 0d327718a484e27beea262644343676ab37d6d890fe7a38ddbea0b089dc81790 | FY2023 to FY2025 statements, FY2024 and FY2025 balance sheets, debt, lease and liquidity notes, segment note, forward cash estimates |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

The document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing. Nothing in the run settings is an issuer source.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Zebra's leverage on trailing unadjusted EBITDA fell to 2.25x total debt and 2.09x net debt at October 3, 2026, but USD 2,077 million of debt falls due within a year, so creditors rely on the planned refinancing more than on the ratio.

Trailing EBITDA rose from USD 885 million in FY2025 to USD 1,141 million, helped by the Elo Touch acquisition and a tariff refund benefit of about USD 73 million in the second quarter of 2026, while debt carried on the balance sheet rose from USD 2,502 million to USD 2,571 million. Zebra states no EBITDA of its own, so every ratio uses operating income plus depreciation and amortization with no add-backs, and interest cover is 7.66x on USD 149 million of trailing cash interest.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5, 13–15, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–76; calculation C082; calculation C083; calculation C084; calculation C033; calculation C039; calculation C051; calculation C054; calculation C105
### Leverage and coverage

Leverage has fallen from 3.38x total debt at FY2023 to 2.38x at FY2024, risen to 2.83x at FY2025 and fallen again to 2.25x on a trailing basis at October 3, 2026. The FY2025 rise follows the acquisitions of Elo Touch and Photoneo, which took USD 1,365 million of cash and were funded from cash that had built up to USD 901 million at FY2024 and from revolver borrowings, so net leverage moved from 1.39x to 2.69x. The 2026 fall comes from earnings, not repayment: total debt is USD 69 million higher than at FY2025, while trailing EBITDA is USD 256 million higher, so deleveraging depends on the earnings base holding.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–76; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C067; calculation C070; calculation C073; calculation C071; calculation C074; calculation C111; calculation C112

Reported EBITDA contains items that flatter or depress it. The trailing figure includes a tariff refund benefit of about USD 73 million recognized in cost of sales in the second quarter of 2026; without it trailing EBITDA would be USD 1,068 million and leverage 2.41x total debt and 2.24x net debt (an Analyst Judgement sensitivity, not used in any ratio). FY2025 EBITDA is after exit and restructuring costs of USD 76 million, including USD 45 million of impairments, so the FY2025 base is also not clean. Zebra states no adjusted EBITDA, so no bridge is drawn and none of these items is added back.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 59, 74; calculation C105; calculation C106; calculation C107

Interest cover is 5.92x at FY2023, 16.62x at FY2024, 6.86x at FY2025 and 7.66x on a trailing basis. The FY2024 figure is not comparable: cash interest paid of USD 55 million in FY2024 is described as inclusive or net of forward interest rate swaps, and that year also shows USD 86 million of cash receipts on forward swaps, while net interest expense was USD 98 million. Cash interest rose to USD 99 million in the first nine months of 2026 from USD 79 million a year earlier as borrowings grew, and a refinancing at current market rates could raise it further, because the term loan and revolver carry floating rates near 5.25% and the notes 6.5%.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 74–76, 95; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 13–15; calculation C069; calculation C072; calculation C075; calculation C084
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow of USD 711 million in the first nine months of 2026 against EBITDA of USD 943 million converts well, and free cash flow after USD 50 million of capital expenditure was USD 661 million; the conversion is helped by about USD 73 million of tariff refunds, of which USD 46 million has been received in cash and USD 27 million sits in receivables. Working capital absorbed cash: receivables rose to USD 1,025 million from USD 801 million and inventories to USD 851 million from USD 729 million as sales grew, partly offset by higher payables. The consequence for creditors is that cash generation is strong but is being returned to shareholders: repurchases of USD 643 million equal 97.28% of free cash flow, and the shortfall was met by net borrowing of USD 67 million, so free cash flow has not reduced debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 16, 26; calculation C103; calculation C104; calculation C110; calculation C113; calculation C115
### Liquidity and refinancing

Cash of USD 182 million and revolver availability of USD 1,045 million after letters of credit give liquidity of USD 1,227 million at October 3, 2026, but every bank facility matures within about eight months: the receivables facility on March 19, 2027 and the term loan and the revolver on May 25, 2027. The balance sheet therefore classes USD 2,077 million of debt as current, against USD 141 million at FY2025, and the 2027 maturity of USD 2,056 million is the term loan balance after one more installment plus the revolver and receivables borrowings. The revolver availability disappears when the revolver matures, so committed liquidity beyond May 2027 is cash alone until a refinancing is signed. Management states it intends to refinance the credit facility in the fourth quarter of 2026, after saying in its second quarter report that it would do so in the second half of 2026; the sources hold nothing dated after November 3, 2026, so the outcome is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13–15, 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C108; calculation C109; calculation C054
### Data quality and definitions

Several definition points limit comparability. EBITDA is derived because Zebra states none, as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, and quarterly depreciation for the second and third quarters is obtained by difference because the cash flow statements are cumulative. Debt facility amounts in the debt note are called carrying value but are before USD 6 million of issuance costs and USD 1 million of discounts that the note deducts in total, so the balance sheet total of USD 2,571 million is used as Total Debt and the facility total of USD 2,578 million is kept as principal. Segments were realigned in the fourth quarter of 2025 to Connected Frontline and Asset Visibility & Automation and share-based compensation was removed from segment income, so FY2022 segment data are on the former basis and are not shown. The 2026 reports state that prior-period operating cash flow amounts were reclassified without giving amounts, and the cover of the FY2025 annual report checks the box for correction of an error without describing one, although the key FY2024 totals agree between the two annual reports.

Two items are credit-relevant funding that is not debt. Deferred revenue of USD 852 million (current USD 438 million and long-term USD 414 million) is stable against USD 842 million at FY2025 and is a prepayment obligation to customers rather than payables. Receivables factoring of up to EUR 150 million removes receivables from the balance sheet, with USD 22 million of sold receivables uncollected and USD 63 million of collections not yet remitted to the bank at October 3, 2026, so the off-balance-sheet funding is small relative to debt but the remittance liability falls inside accrued liabilities.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 15, 18; calculation C116

Subsequent events are flagged and kept out of period figures. After FY2025 the board authorized repurchases of up to USD 1 billion on February 4, 2026 and about USD 100 million of shares were bought by February 5, 2026; the first quarter report adds about USD 200 million bought after its quarter end. All of these fall inside the 2026 interim statements and are not applied to FY2025 net debt, so no pro forma figure is established for FY2025. For the latest balance sheet the share count on the cover fell between October 3 and October 27, 2026 without an amount being stated, so no adjustment is drawn.

## Gaps

- High: No adjusted EBITDA, reconciliation or add-back schedule is printed in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived and unadjusted; this restricts every leverage and interest cover figure and the whole adjusted bridge. Action: obtain management earnings releases if an adjusted view is wanted.

- High: Covenant ratio levels, definitions and headroom are not printed; the notes say only that financial ratios are maintained at designated levels and that the issuer complied at October 3, 2026. This restricts any covenant or headroom conclusion. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and amendments.

- High: Security and legal rank of the term loan and the revolver, and the identity of the guarantors and co-issuers, are not stated, so no ranked debt stack or cumulative leverage is drawn and the debt perimeter is stated at group level only. Action: obtain the credit agreement, the indenture and the subsidiary list.

- High: Nothing dated after November 3, 2026 was supplied, while management intends to refinance the credit facility in the fourth quarter of 2026; any refinancing after that date is not reflected in debt, maturities or liquidity. Action: check for a financing announcement dated November 3 to November 18, 2026.

- Medium: The FY2024 cash interest of USD 55 million is labelled net of forward interest rate swaps and the year shows USD 86 million of cash receipts on forward swaps, so the FY2024 interest cover of 16.62x is not comparable with other years. Action: use FY2023, FY2025 and the trailing figure for trend.

- Medium: Trailing EBITDA includes a tariff refund benefit of about USD 73 million and FY2025 EBITDA is after USD 76 million of exit and restructuring costs; no adjusted measure exists to separate them. Action: show the sensitivity beside the ratios.

- Medium: The 2026 reports state that prior-period operating cash flow amounts were reclassified without amounts, so 2025 interim operating cash flow cannot be bridged to the originally reported figures. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly reports as originally filed.

- Medium: The cover of the FY2025 annual report checks the box for correction of an error and no correction is described; FY2024 totals agree with the 2024 annual report for the lines compared. Action: confirm whether any comparative was revised.

- Medium: Quarterly depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation and cash flows for the second and third quarters are not printed alone, so quarterly EBITDA for those quarters is derived by difference and quarterly cash flow columns are not shown. Action: none needed for annual and trailing analysis.

- Medium: Segment data for FY2022 are on the former AIT and EVM basis and are shown as not supplied; the fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed alone and no fourth quarter column is built. Action: use the current basis only.

- Medium: The first quarter, six months and nine months of 2026 are 6 days longer than the same periods of 2025, so every trailing figure covers 371 days rather than 365 and no day adjustment is made; this overstates trailing flows by up to 1.64% against a twelve month period. This qualifies the source readiness statement that a trailing twelve months can be formed: it can be formed, but it covers 371 days. Action: state the period length beside any trailing ratio.
- Low: Revolver availability at 2023-12-31 is not stated in the 2024 annual report, so FY2023 undrawn committed facilities are not supplied. Action: none needed for the current liquidity view.

- Low: Annual amortization of the term loan is described as quarterly installments without an amount; the maturity table shows USD 22 million due in the last three months of 2026. Action: obtain the credit agreement for the schedule.
- Low: The reference rate and margin of each floating facility are not stated by instrument; the annual report says exposure is primarily to SOFR. Action: obtain the credit agreement.

- Low: Carrying values by instrument are not stated because the note deducts issuance costs and discounts in total; the financing cost adjustment row carries USD 7 million at October 3, 2026. Action: none needed.
- Low: The maturity table prints dashes for 2028, 2029 and 2030 and no row is drawn for them; the rows drawn add to total debt principal. Action: none needed.

- Low: Dashes are printed for lines with no amount, including exit and restructuring costs in several periods, foreign exchange in the first quarter of 2026, debt issuance costs in FY2023 and FY2025 and the effect of exchange rates on cash in FY2023 and FY2022; they are carried as not supplied, not as zero, and no total depends on them. Action: none needed.

- Low: Lease liabilities of USD 205 million at October 3, 2026 sit on their own balance sheet lines and are not part of Total Debt or net debt, and fixed purchase commitments are outside debt as well. Action: treat them as claims outside debt in the liquidity and credit views.
- Low: Earnings per share, share counts and region data are printed in the filings but are not carried in the statement tables. Action: none needed for credit analysis.

- Low: Capital expenditure is not split into maintenance and growth, and unlevered free cash flow is not stated; free cash flow is the issuer's definition of operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Action: none needed.

spans.text: # Zebra Technologies Corp: business and governance
## Request

Business and governance review of Zebra Technologies Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: operating model, ownership and control, transactions, capital allocation and disclosure quality from the five supplied SEC filings, through the quarter ended October 3, 2026.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2025-02-13 | 6ded346d307a4e9b452e3151403c22db30e3a9b441a07cc7905331757a65fbde | Matrox purchase, the 2024 senior notes issue, the Photoneo agreement, repurchases in 2023 and 2024 and the former segment basis |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2026-02-12 | 0d327718a484e27beea262644343676ab37d6d890fe7a38ddbea0b089dc81790 | Business description, customers, risk factors, acquisitions, liquidity and capital allocation, debt note, segment note, cover page, Part III references and exhibit index |

| 10-Q_2026-04-04_zbra-20260404.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 4, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-05-12 | 0a357fa8e3aff9f314476fa18cb37e956524b11033c869c5e761877fa71a4c1f | Robotics sale, the first-quarter statement that borrowing was raised to fund repurchases |

| 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 4, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-08-04 | edcc3112cdd3d3bd5ee2d37b928c62642ae59455e8f8c32672c24c89bee46fae | Tariff refund recognition, the first-half statement on borrowing and repurchases, the refinancing intention for the second half of 2026 |

| 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 3, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-11-03 | 7b8fe3f783c1f57e1ce6eedc2ac3644a346aca4116b259796349fd7e707f2db7 | Nine-month results, segments, debt, the final Elo allocation, share count, repurchases and the refinancing intention for the fourth quarter of 2026 |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 67b9c1309e2371b2fc8780d15ebbb3a3fe3a9148ba62c491c240fbf3c3e95606 | Source inventory, dated events, source limits and the list of what the sources do not supply |
The document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing. Nothing in the run settings is an issuer source.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Zebra is a widely held hardware group with no sponsor named, so creditor risk comes from management's cash use: buybacks were partly debt-funded while USD 2,077 million of debt falls due within a year, and the refinancing is intended, not signed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation BG-8; calculation BG-11

Buybacks of USD 643 million in the first nine months of 2026 equalled 97.3% of free cash flow of USD 661 million, and exceeded all of it once USD 46 million of one-off tariff refund cash is removed. Three distributors bought 59% of 2025 net sales, so one customer's purchasing or credit matters more than the product mix suggests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 21, 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 109; calculation BG-9; calculation BG-13; calculation BG-1
### Key findings

Customer concentration is the largest operating risk: three distributors bought 59% of 2025 net sales, up from 44% in 2023, and the largest took 29%. The same three owed 58% of receivables at the end of 2025, so a purchasing cut or credit event at one of them would reduce sales and slow collections at the same time, and could erode the receivable base that backs the secured receivables facility. The filings name neither the distributors nor their contract terms, so contract length and termination rights are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 39, 109; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation BG-1; calculation BG-14

Recurring revenue gives some visibility but little protection: services and software were 18.1% of 2025 net sales and fell to 16.1% in the first nine months of 2026 as hardware grew faster. Deferred revenue of USD 852 million and remaining contract value of USD 1.14 billion over about two years support service cash flow, while the 81.9% hardware majority depends on component costs and customer demand; the third-quarter gross margin fell to 45.7% from 48.0% on memory costs and mix.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 22; calculation BG-2

Reported growth overstates underlying growth: nine-month 2026 net sales rose 19.0%, but organic growth was 8.3%, with acquisitions and disposals adding 8.5 percentage points and currency 2.2 percentage points. The acquired growth sits mostly in the Connected Frontline segment, whose organic growth was 8.9%, while Asset Visibility and Automation grew 7.7% organically; the profit on the acquired sales is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; calculation BG-5; calculation BG-4

Acquisitions have made the balance sheet intangible-heavy: goodwill and other intangibles of USD 5,385 million are 61.1% of total assets and equity after deducting them is negative USD 1,817 million, so creditor protection rests on cash flow and working capital, not tangible assets. Elo cost USD 1,303 million in cash, 98.0% of it goodwill and acquired intangibles, or 3.2x its implied annual sales of about USD 411 million, and its own profit is not disclosed; the auditor names the valuation of its technology and customer relationships as a critical matter.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72, 88–89; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8; calculation BG-6; calculation BG-7

Buybacks are the main discretionary claim on cash and have been partly debt-funded: repurchases rose from USD 47 million in 2024 to USD 587 million in 2025 and USD 643 million in the first nine months of 2026, and Zebra states that it raised revolver and receivables borrowing to fund them in the first quarter and again in the first half of 2026. Debt principal rose from USD 2,183 million at the end of 2024 to USD 2,578 million at October 3, 2026, USD 616 million of authorization remains, the program can be changed or stopped at any time, and no dividend has been declared since 1991.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57, 65–66; 10-Q_2026-04-04_zbra-20260404.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 31; calculation BG-8; calculation BG-10

Governance risk is medium on mixed evidence: Zebra names no sponsor, pays no dividend, shows no related-party items in its statements and carries unqualified audit opinions on its accounts and internal control, but the proxy statement and the credit documents that would show board control and payment limits are not supplied. The cover of the 2025 annual report ticks the box for correction of an error in prior statements without describing one, so whether any figure was revised is not established.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is cash generation: free cash flow was USD 661 million in the first nine months of 2026, up USD 157 million, debt principal rose only USD 67 million since the end of 2025, cash rose to USD 182 million, the revolver had USD 1,045 million available, and Zebra states it complied with all debt covenants at October 3, 2026. Organic growth of 8.3%, a USD 73 million tariff refund and no disclosed dividend, sponsor fee or related-party leakage all point to a company that can fund both buybacks and a refinancing from operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 14–16, 26; calculation BG-9; calculation BG-10; calculation BG-13

What would strengthen the view: a signed refinancing that extends the term loan and revolver beyond 2027 with disclosed covenant levels, a stated buyback policy tied to leverage, and a proxy statement and credit agreements showing no controlling holder and tight payment limits. What would weaken it: buybacks above free cash flow before the refinancing closes, another debt-funded acquisition, a refinancing that is secured, shorter or more restrictive than the present facilities, or evidence that a leading distributor is cutting purchases.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, holders above a reporting threshold and related-party dealings are not established; the finding that no controlling holder exists would change if a concentrated holder or a related-party arrangement appears.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 115

- The credit agreement, indenture and receivables financing agreement are not supplied, so the baskets that govern buybacks, acquisitions, liens and new debt are not established (the notes are said only to limit liens, subsidiary guarantees and mergers); the medium governance rating rests on observed behavior and would move to low or high if the documents show tight or loose payment limits.

- Distributor identities and contract terms are not supplied, so the concentration finding cannot be tested for contract length, exclusivity or termination rights; long-term contracts would lower the concentration risk.
- No evidence is dated after November 3, 2026, so a refinancing, new buyback commitment or acquisition announced since then would change the view on maturity dependence and capital allocation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 32

- Elo's own earnings, integration costs and synergies are not disclosed, so whether the purchase supports the debt it added is not established, and the 3.2x implied sales multiple cannot be set against profit; a profit disclosure could move the acquisition finding in either direction.
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
### Company and operating model
| Item | What the filings state | Why it matters to creditors | Source |

| What Zebra sells | Mobile computers, barcode and card printers, scanners, RFID and location systems, machine vision, self-service touchscreens and workflow software, with maintenance, managed services and cloud subscriptions | A broad hardware range with an installed base that creates supplies and service demand, which limits dependence on one product line | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–11 |

| Segments | Connected Frontline USD 2,960 million (54.9%) and Asset Visibility and Automation USD 2,436 million (45.1%) of FY2025 net sales of USD 5,396 million; segment operating income USD 585 million and USD 514 million | Two segments of similar size; Connected Frontline carries the Elo acquisition and Asset Visibility and Automation earns the higher margin | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109 |

| Revenue model | Tangible products USD 4,418 million (81.9%) and services and software USD 978 million (18.1%) in FY2025; deferred revenue USD 852 million and remaining performance obligations USD 1.14 billion, recognised over about two years, at 2026-10-03 | About a fifth of sales is contracted and recurring; the rest depends on customer demand | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8 |

| Customers and channel | Sold mainly through two-tier distribution, value added resellers, software vendors, direct marketers and original equipment manufacturers; three distributors took 29%, 15% and 15% of FY2025 net sales | Sales, receivables and the pledged receivables base rest on a few counterparties | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16 |

| Supply chain | Final assembly by contract manufacturers in China, Malaysia, Vietnam, Taiwan and Mexico; supplies made in the U.S., Mexico and Europe; some components are sole-sourced; multi-year purchase commitments of about USD 101 million at 2025-12-31 | Component cost and tariff shocks reach gross margin first, and fixed purchase commitments reduce flexibility if demand falls | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66 |

| Geography and currency | North America 49.9%, EMEA 31.9%, Asia-Pacific 11.4% and Latin America 6.7% of FY2025 net sales; U.S. 49.0% and Germany 16.0%; euro cash flow hedges of EUR 648 million at 2026-10-03; a one percentage point currency move changes pre-tax income by about USD 2 million | Half of sales are outside the U.S.; euro exposure is hedged and the stated currency sensitivity is small | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 109–110; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 12 |

| Margin and cost | Gross margin 49.4% in nine months 2026, including a USD 73 million tariff refund benefit, and 45.7% in the third quarter against 48.0% a year earlier on memory costs and mix; research and development USD 593 million, 11.0% of FY2025 net sales | Component prices feed through to margin; the refund is a one-time recovery, so nine-month margin overstates the run rate | 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17 |

| Cash conversion | Operating cash flow USD 711 million and free cash flow USD 661 million in nine months 2026; FY2025 free cash flow USD 831 million; capex USD 86 million in FY2025 and an expected USD 85 million to USD 95 million in 2026 | Low capital intensity turns profit into cash, which is why both buybacks and debt service can be funded | 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66 |
### Company profile
| Item | Detail | Source |
| Legal name and form | Zebra Technologies Corporation, a Delaware corporation; commission file number 000-19406 | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 1 |
| Headquarters | 3 Overlook Point, Lincolnshire, Illinois, United States | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 1 |
| Listing and filer status | Class A Common Stock on the NASDAQ Stock Market under ZBRA; large accelerated filer | 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 1 |

| Shares and holders | 47,087,454 Class A shares outstanding at 2026-10-27 and 49,191,704 at 2026-02-05; 72 holders of record; market value held by non-affiliates USD 15.5 billion at 2025-06-28 | 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56 |

| Ownership and control | No controlling holder or sponsor is named; holder percentages and director information are incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not supplied | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 115 |

| Segments | Connected Frontline and Asset Visibility and Automation since the fourth quarter of 2025; the chief executive officer is the chief operating decision maker | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 19 |

| Employees and footprint | About 10,700 employees in 57 countries, 44% in the U.S.; 126 leased facilities and 3 owned laboratory and warehouse facilities; offerings sold in about 179 countries | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70 |

| Auditor | Ernst & Young LLP, Chicago, auditor since 2005; unqualified opinions on the FY2025 statements and on internal control over financial reporting | 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–73 |

| Fiscal calendar | Fiscal year ends 2025-12-31; the 2026 quarters ended 2026-04-04, 2026-07-04 and 2026-10-03 | 10-Q_2026-04-04_zbra-20260404.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 1 |
| Credit ratings | Not supplied: no rating report or rating statement is in the supplied sources | Run settings (not issuer evidence) |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No transaction is pending in the supplied filings. Elo Holdings was bought on September 30, 2025 for USD 1,303 million in cash, net of cash acquired, after a purchase agreement dated August 3, 2025; Photoneo was bought on February 28, 2025 for USD 62 million after an agreement signed on December 27, 2024 at about EUR 60 million; and the robotics automation business was sold to Skild AI in the first quarter of 2026 for USD 20 million of consideration, of which USD 9 million was cash, with a net pre-tax gain of USD 5 million.

Elo and Photoneo were funded with cash and revolver borrowing: Zebra states that it increased revolver borrowing in the fourth quarter of 2025 to help fund Elo, and in 2025 it raised USD 347 million of debt and repaid USD 19 million while cash fell from USD 901 million to USD 125 million. The Elo purchase price allocation became final on October 3, 2026 after USD 4 million of adjustments to goodwill and deferred tax liabilities.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 73, 75; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation BG-9; calculation BG-6

The filings describe no new debt instrument since the USD 500 million 6.5% senior notes due June 1, 2032, issued in the second quarter of 2024 for net proceeds of about USD 492 million; later borrowing was drawn under existing facilities, taking the revolver from nil at the end of 2024 to USD 445 million at October 3, 2026. Management intends to refinance the term loan and revolver, which mature on May 25, 2027, in the fourth quarter of 2026, but the filings state no lender, amount, structure or terms, and the separate receivables facility, with a USD 180 million limit and USD 124 million drawn, matures on March 19, 2027.

spans.text: # Zebra Technologies Corp: fundamental credit
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Zebra Technologies Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business quality, financial profile, refinancing capacity, financial policy and the main downside path from the five supplied SEC filings and the accepted Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance work, through the quarter ended October 3, 2026.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2025-02-13 | 6ded346d307a4e9b452e3151403c22db30e3a9b441a07cc7905331757a65fbde | The 2024 senior notes issue and 2023 and 2024 history |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, audited by Ernst & Young LLP | 2026-02-12 | 0d327718a484e27beea262644343676ab37d6d890fe7a38ddbea0b089dc81790 | Business, competition, customers, risk factors, suppliers, liquidity statements, debt and segment notes |

| 10-Q_2026-04-04_zbra-20260404.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 4, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-05-12 | 0a357fa8e3aff9f314476fa18cb37e956524b11033c869c5e761877fa71a4c1f | First-quarter statement that borrowing was raised to fund repurchases |

| 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 4, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-08-04 | edcc3112cdd3d3bd5ee2d37b928c62642ae59455e8f8c32672c24c89bee46fae | Price realization against memory costs and the first-half funding statement |

| 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 3, 2026 (unaudited) | 2026-11-03 | 7b8fe3f783c1f57e1ce6eedc2ac3644a346aca4116b259796349fd7e707f2db7 | Nine-month results, balance sheet, debt, liquidity, segments, tariff refund and the refinancing intention |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 67b9c1309e2371b2fc8780d15ebbb3a3fe3a9148ba62c491c240fbf3c3e95606 | Source inventory, source limits and the list of absent inputs |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | CP-1 | ce8643cc37ce94d2eb1faa5f1adb489a422494a022480398a7424ab0693f1c9d | Trailing EBITDA, leverage, interest cover, free cash flow, liquidity and the maturity ladder |

| Business & governance (CP-1A) | CP-1A | 6b496c2ee837c5e029f8639826ed13605138161482423e49aa276b9afc4dde57 | Business model, customer concentration, transactions, capital allocation and the governance risk level |
The document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing. Nothing in the run settings is an issuer source.
## Findings
### Bottom line
Zebra's business and cash generation support its debt, but credit quality is constrained by a refinancing that must close before May 2027 and by buybacks that absorb nearly all free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 26; calculation FC-4; calculation FC-6

Trailing unadjusted EBITDA of USD 1,141 million gives leverage of 2.25x total debt and 2.09x net debt with interest cover of 7.66x, so operating risk is moderate; the larger uncertainty is USD 2,077 million of current debt, against liquidity of USD 1,227 million that falls to cash of USD 182 million when the revolver matures on May 25, 2027.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 14, 26; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2
### Key findings

Refinancing, not operations, is the central credit issue: USD 2,077 million of debt is current at October 3, 2026, 80.6% of principal matures by May 25, 2027, and liquidity of USD 1,227 million is mostly revolver availability of USD 1,045 million that ends with that maturity. Management intends to refinance in the fourth quarter of 2026, but no lender, amount or terms are stated, so creditors are exposed to the market window and to the terms Zebra accepts. Current debt is 2.10x trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million, which makes repayment from cash flow a fallback that works only if buybacks stop.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13–14, 26; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC-2; calculation FC-3; calculation FC-4

Leverage is moderate on a reported basis but rests on an earnings base helped by one-offs: trailing EBITDA of USD 1,141 million includes a USD 73 million tariff refund benefit, and without it EBITDA is USD 1,068 million with leverage of 2.41x total debt and 2.24x net debt. Third-quarter gross margin of 45.7% was 230 bp below a year earlier on memory costs and mix, and at that margin across the trailing year EBITDA would be USD 197 million lower, lifting leverage to 2.72x total debt and 2.53x net debt with interest cover of 6.34x; this is an illustrative sensitivity, not a forecast.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 21–22; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-7

Cash generation is the main support but it is being returned to shareholders: trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million is 86.59% of EBITDA, yet repurchases of USD 643 million in the first nine months of 2026 equalled 97.28% of free cash flow of USD 661 million and 104.55% of it once USD 46 million of tariff refund cash is excluded. Debt carried on the balance sheet still rose USD 69 million in 2026 and cash interest rose 25.3% to USD 99 million, so free cash flow has not reduced debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 21, 26; calculation FC-5; calculation FC-6; calculation FC-10

Customer concentration and cost shocks are the operating risks that could break the cash flow: three distributors bought 59% of 2025 net sales and owed 58% of receivables, and the filings name neither the distributors nor their contract terms. Memory costs and tariffs reach gross margin before Zebra can reprice, and services and software, the only contracted revenue, were 18.1% of 2025 net sales.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 42–43, 109; calculation FC-11; calculation FC-14

The balance sheet offers little tangible protection: goodwill and other intangibles of USD 5,385 million are 61.1% of total assets and equity after deducting them is negative USD 1,817 million, and the Elo purchase of USD 1,303 million is 98.0% goodwill and intangibles at 3.2x implied annual sales with no disclosed profit. Creditors therefore rely on cash flow and on the receivables and inventory behind the facilities, and USD 868 million of receivables are pledged to the receivables facility against USD 124 million borrowed.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 15; calculation FC-12; calculation FC-13; calculation FC-15

Financial policy is the main discretionary risk and carries medium risk: no sponsor, dividend or related-party leakage is evidenced, but management has funded buybacks partly with revolver and receivables borrowing while the credit facility approached maturity, and the credit documents that would show payment limits are not supplied. Growth supports the earnings base meanwhile: organic growth was 8.3% in the first nine months of 2026 and operating income rose 37.8%.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-04-04_zbra-20260404.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation FC-14; calculation FC-17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that leverage and cover are moderate and cash generation is large: net leverage of 2.09x, interest cover of 7.66x and trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million, which would repay the current debt in about two years if buybacks stopped. Zebra also issued USD 500 million of senior notes in 2024, states compliance with all debt covenants at October 3, 2026, has revolver availability of USD 1,045 million until May 2027 and has declared no dividend since 1991, so near-term liquidity is not stretched before the revolver matures and the risk is concentrated in the refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_zbra-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-4

What would strengthen the view: a signed refinancing that extends the term loan and revolver well beyond 2027 with covenant levels disclosed and no added security, a stated buyback policy tied to leverage, and credit documents that limit payments to shareholders. What would weaken it: no signed refinancing by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026, buybacks above free cash flow, a debt-funded acquisition, gross margin below the third-quarter level of 45.7%, or a purchasing cut by one of the three distributors.
### Limitations

- No rating, bond price or peer data is supplied, so refinancing access is judged from the 2024 notes issue and management's statements only; market data showing wide spreads or a closed window would lower the refinancing view, and tight spreads would raise it.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Trailing EBITDA is derived from reported lines with no add-backs and includes a tariff refund benefit of USD 73 million; Zebra states no adjusted EBITDA, so leverage on a management basis could differ and the leverage support in this view rests on an unadjusted figure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Covenant levels, definitions and headroom are not supplied, so the distance to a breach cannot be judged and the financial policy view rests on behavior; covenant analysis belongs to Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity, which are not part of this run.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15

- The refinancing is the pivot of this view and nothing dated after November 3, 2026 is supplied, so a facility signed since then would shift the weight from the maturity wall to the cost of the new terms.

- Management gives no sales or earnings outlook in the supplied filings beyond capital expenditure, debt payment and restructuring estimates, so the outlook and downside sections rest on reported trends and a sensitivity, not on guidance; a guidance range could move the downside path in either direction.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths, ranked by their weight in the credit view:

1. Cash generation and moderate leverage are the main support: trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million and net leverage of 2.09x give room to service debt and, if buybacks stopped, to repay the current debt in about two years.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC-1; calculation FC-4

2. Breadth of products, regions and contracted revenue limits single-line shocks: two segments of similar size, 49.0% of sales in the U.S. and 18.1% from services and software with USD 852 million of deferred revenue.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC-14
3. Low capital intensity and an outsourced assembly model keep cash conversion high: capex was about 1.6% of 2025 net sales and free cash flow was 86.59% of trailing EBITDA.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 75; calculation FC-5
4. The absence of a sponsor, dividend and related-party items removes owner-directed leakage, so shareholder returns come through buybacks that the board can change at any time.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57, 65; calculation FC-17
Weaknesses, ranked by their weight in the credit view:
1. Refinancing dependence is the main weakness: USD 2,077 million of current debt, 80.6% of principal due by May 25, 2027, and revolver availability that ends with that maturity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13–14, 26; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-3
2. Buybacks near free cash flow have kept debt from falling: repurchases of USD 643 million were 97.28% of nine-month free cash flow and were partly funded by borrowing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 26; 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation FC-6; calculation FC-10
3. Customer concentration puts earnings and collections on a few counterparties: three distributors bought 59% of 2025 net sales and owed 58% of receivables.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 109; calculation FC-11
4. Margin exposure and a thin tangible base add risk: third-quarter gross margin fell to 45.7% from 48.0% on memory costs, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 5,385 million are 61.1% of total assets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 22; calculation FC-7; calculation FC-12
### Company description

Zebra designs and sells, through contract manufacturers, mobile computers, barcode and card printers, scanners, RFID and location systems, machine vision and self-service touchscreens with related software, supplies and services; FY2025 net sales were USD 5,396 million, split between Connected Frontline at USD 2,960 million and Asset Visibility and Automation at USD 2,436 million. The range and an installed base that pulls through supplies and services support cash-flow visibility, but 81.9% of sales are hardware and three distributors take 59% of sales, so visibility is partial and concentration limits it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–11, 109; calculation FC-11; calculation FC-14

Recent growth was bought rather than built: Elo for USD 1,303 million in September 2025, Photoneo for USD 62 million in February 2025 and a sale of the robotics business in the first quarter of 2026, with segments realigned in the fourth quarter of 2025 so that segment history starts at FY2023. The consequence for creditors is higher intangibles and integration risk, and a debt-funded step up that has to be refinanced in 2027.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 88–89; calculation FC-13
### Ownership and group structure

Zebra is a Delaware corporation with one class of listed common stock and no sponsor or controlling holder named; holder percentages, board composition and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the guarantors of the senior notes are described only as certain subsidiaries. Without a sponsor there is no equity cure or extraction risk, leverage tolerance is revealed by the board's buyback authorizations, and the group structure includes a receivables financing subsidiary named in the exhibits, with lenders to the receivables facility holding first-priority security over U.S. receivables.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 115; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation FC-15
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is a mix of cyclical hardware demand and contracted services and software; deferred revenue of USD 852 million and USD 1.14 billion of remaining performance obligations over about two years give visibility for services but not for hardware orders, whose backlog Zebra says is not a reliable indicator. Pricing power is partial: in the second quarter Zebra says it fully mitigated higher memory costs through price realization, yet in the third quarter gross margin fell 230 bp on memory costs and mix, so pricing has not kept pace with cost in every quarter. Organic growth was 8.3% in nine months 2026 with both segments growing, which supports the earnings base, but concentration in three distributors means a single buyer's decision can move revenue and collections together.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-04_zbra-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 21–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation FC-11; calculation FC-14
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Assembly is outsourced, so product costs flex with volume, but operating expenses, including research and development of USD 593 million or 11.0% of FY2025 net sales, are a largely fixed base that deleverages if sales fall. Margins can be defended against modest cost inflation through pricing, as the second quarter showed, but the third-quarter decline and the one-time USD 73 million tariff refund show that reported margins are not a clean run rate; the 2025 Productivity Plan is substantially complete, so little further cost relief is available. The consequence is that a margin squeeze would reach EBITDA quickly: the sensitivity at the third-quarter margin lowers trailing EBITDA by USD 197 million.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16, 21–22; calculation FC-7
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low: capex was 1.6% of 2025 net sales and USD 85 million to USD 95 million is expected for 2026, so free cash flow converts 86.59% of trailing EBITDA. Working capital absorbed cash in 2026 as receivables rose to USD 1,025 million from USD 801 million and inventories to USD 851 million from USD 729 million, and operating cash flow includes USD 46 million of tariff refund cash with USD 27 million still in receivables. Free cash flow is therefore strong but partly one-time, and it is available to repay debt only if buybacks give way to the refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16, 26; calculation FC-5
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense among large named competitors in each category, yet gross margin held at 46% to 48% from FY2023 to FY2025, which shows stable pricing over the cycle; the credit risk is the third-quarter margin decline, not a lasting loss of position. Entry barriers rest on channel relationships and installed-base switching costs, which management asserts and the stable margins support. Substitution by tablets and smartphones exists for some mobile computing uses and limits pricing in that segment. Buyer power is the sharpest force because three distributors take 59% of sales, and supplier power matters through sole-source components, memory costs and multi-year purchase commitments of about USD 101 million, so cost pass-through, not demand, is the main margin risk.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14–15, 42, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC-11
### PEST analysis

Trade policy is the one macro factor that materially alters earnings and cash: Zebra imports a significant share of its offerings into the U.S., a Supreme Court ruling in February 2026 invalidated certain tariffs, and a USD 73 million refund benefit was recognised, of which USD 27 million is uncollected. Interest rates matter because USD 2,078 million of principal floats, so a 100 bp rise adds USD 20.8 million a year and takes interest cover from 7.66x to 6.72x; currency is hedged for euro sales with a stated one percentage point sensitivity of about USD 2 million of pre-tax income. Technology transitions in Wi-Fi, 5G, Android and imaging create demand but also product cost, and no other political, social or regulatory factor is shown to alter credit quality.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 43, 70; 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; calculation FC-8
### SWOT analysis

Strengths that support creditors are cash generation, moderate leverage, breadth of products and regions and low capital intensity. Weaknesses that constrain them are the 2027 maturity wall, buybacks near free cash flow, customer concentration and an intangible-heavy balance sheet. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a signed refinancing with a longer maturity, a buyback policy tied to leverage, and growth in services and machine vision that raises contracted revenue. Threats that could weaken it are a purchasing cut by a leading distributor, memory costs and tariffs, a slow or costly refinancing, and an impairment of the Elo intangibles.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC-2; calculation FC-6; calculation FC-11; calculation FC-12
### Financial profile and credit quality

The main credit supports are trailing free cash flow of USD 988 million, net leverage of 2.09x, interest cover of 7.66x and liquidity of USD 1,227 million; the constraints are the USD 2,077 million of current debt, buybacks near free cash flow and a margin base helped by a one-time refund. The trend is improving on earnings and flat on debt: trailing EBITDA is up 28.93% on FY2025 and trailing revenue up 13.81%, while carrying debt rose USD 69 million in 2026. Key missing datapoints are covenant levels, the refinancing terms, distributor contract terms and Elo's own earnings, which keeps the financial policy and refinancing conclusions provisional.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-5; calculation FC-10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the outcome that matters is the refinancing: a signed facility removes the maturity wall, while a delay pushes the decision toward the 2027 dates when the revolver availability of USD 1,045 million is about to end. Company tailwinds are organic growth of 8.3%, broad-based growth across regions and verticals, completed cost actions and low capex of USD 85 million to USD 95 million; headwinds are memory costs, tariff exposure, distributor concentration and USD 616 million of remaining buyback authorization that can be used at any time. Over three to five years the technology transitions in mobile computing, imaging and RFID and growth in services and software are the supports, but no sales or earnings outlook is supplied, so the medium-term view is directional only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 22, 26, 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_zbra-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 66; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-14
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario starts with a purchasing cut or credit event at one of the three distributors while memory costs hold gross margin near the third-quarter level of 45.7% and the debt market is slow or costly in the first half of 2027. The first operating break is sales and collections falling together, because the same distributors owed 58% of receivables, so working capital absorbs cash as it did in 2026 and free cash flow drops below the pace of buybacks. At the third-quarter margin alone trailing EBITDA is USD 197 million lower, leverage is 2.72x total debt and 2.53x net debt with interest cover of 6.34x, and a refinancing priced 100 bp higher on the floating-rate debt adds USD 20.8 million of interest, so that combined interest cover would be 5.56x. The liquidity consequence is that revolver availability ends on May 25, 2027, leaving cash of USD 182 million against USD 2,078 million of principal due by then unless a refinancing is signed. Management can stop buybacks, which have USD 616 million of authorization left, hold capex near USD 85 million to USD 95 million and use factoring, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall on these levers if access to the debt market stays open; the observable trigger is whether a refinancing is signed by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_zbra-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 26, 31; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-3; calculation FC-7; calculation FC-8; calculation FC-11; calculation FC-18
The primary downside path is a distributor or margin shock arriving while the refinancing of the credit facility is still unsigned.
### Overall credit view

Overall, Zebra presents an adequate to strong business profile supported by cash generation, breadth of products and regions and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by near-term maturities and by buybacks that absorb free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears strong because free cash flow is 86.59% of EBITDA, although customer concentration and component costs can move it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the debt market, the covenant and security terms Zebra accepts, and whether it pauses buybacks until the refinancing closes. The primary downside path is a distributor or margin shock before the refinancing is signed. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement, the refinancing terms, distributor contract terms and Elo's own earnings. Top risk: refinancing the credit facility before it matures on May 25, 2027.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-4; calculation FC-5; calculation FC-6
